lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Mastery check: communication and support network

objective: Learners map their real support network by role, such as the adult they would ask about a money question or the adult they would ask about a medical question, without recording any real name, address, phone number, or email address, then identify any gap in the network and a specific step to close it.
scenario: Using only roles and relationships, never real names or contact details, the learner builds a private planning page naming, for at least four different kinds of real needs, the adult they would actually go to and why, then checks the map for a gap, a kind of need with no clear person, and writes a specific step to address it.
safetyNotes: This map uses roles and relationships only, such as 'the adult I would ask about money,' and never records a real name, address, phone number, or email address.
This is a private planning artifact for the learner's own use; it is not shared publicly and is not a contact list.
materials: paper or a document for the private role-based network map

tasks.directions: Brainstorm the different kinds of real needs you might have to ask a trusted adult about.

prompts.text: List at least four different kinds of needs where you'd want to ask a trusted adult (for example, a money question, a medical question, a school problem, or emotional support).

tasks.directions: For at least four kinds of needs, name the adult you would actually go to, described by role or relationship only, never by real name.

prompts.text: I named, by role only, the adult I would ask about a money question.
I named, by role only, the adult I would ask about a medical or health question.
I named, by role only, the adult I would ask about a school or academic problem.
I named, by role only, the trusted adult I would go to for emotional support.

tasks.directions: Check your map for a gap, a kind of need with no clear person, and address it.

prompts.text: Did you find at least one kind of need on your map without a clear person you could name, even just by role?
If you found a gap, name one specific step you could take to fill it. If not, explain how you checked to confirm your network is solid.

tasks.directions: Think about why this map matters going forward.

prompts.text: Explain why having more than one adult you could ask for at least one kind of need matters, even if you already know your first choice well.

remediation: If a learner writes an actual name, address, phone number, or email instead of a role, reteach by having them cross out the identifying detail and replace it with a role-based description (such as 'the adult who handles the household's money questions') before continuing.
extension: Have the learner add a second-choice person for one need, described by role, and explain what they would do if their first-choice adult were unavailable.
